storyTitle: Implement validation rules ensuring mandatory cosmetic classification fields (category, application type) are populated before persistence

functional.title: Successfully save cosmetic classification with both mandatory fields populated
preconditions: User is logged in with a role that has permission to create/edit cosmetic classifications
User is on the Cosmetic Classification form page
The 'Category' dropdown is loaded with valid options (e.g., 'Skin Care', 'Hair Care', 'Oral Hygiene')
The 'Application Type' dropdown is loaded with valid options (e.g., 'Leave-on', 'Rinse-off')

steps.action: Select a value from the 'Category' dropdown (e.g., select 'Skin Care')
steps.expectedResult: 'Skin Care' is displayed as the selected value in the Category field

steps.action: Select a value from the 'Application Type' dropdown (e.g., select 'Leave-on')
steps.expectedResult: 'Leave-on' is displayed as the selected value in the Application Type field

steps.action: Fill in any other required fields on the form with valid data
steps.expectedResult: All fields accept the entered data without errors

steps.action: Click the 'Save' button to persist the cosmetic classification record
steps.expectedResult: The record is saved successfully. A success notification message (e.g., 'Cosmetic classification saved successfully') is displayed. No validation errors appear.

steps.action: Navigate to the saved record or list view and locate the newly created record
steps.expectedResult: The record is visible in the list/detail view with 'Category' = 'Skin Care' and 'Application Type' = 'Leave-on'

postconditions: The cosmetic classification record is persisted in the database with Category = 'Skin Care' and Application Type = 'Leave-on'
User remains on the confirmation or detail page after successful save
An audit trail entry is created for the new record creation

steps.expectedResult: The Category field shows the default placeholder (e.g., '-- Select Category --') with no value selected

steps.action: Click the 'Save' button

postconditions: No record is saved to the database

The validation error message remains visible until the user corrects the field

steps.action: Inspect the response body of the failed API call
steps.expectedResult: The response body contains a validation error message indicating 'Category is required' or similar structured error

steps.expectedResult: The API returns an HTTP 400 or 422 response with a validation error for Application Type

steps.action: Submit a request with both 'category' and 'applicationType' empty
steps.expectedResult: The API returns an HTTP 400 or 422 response with validation errors for both fields

postconditions: No records were persisted in the database from any of the invalid requests

steps.expectedResult: 'Skin Care' is selected and the dropdown closes. The Category field displays 'Skin Care'. Focus remains on the Category field.

steps.action: Press Space or Enter to open the dropdown again, then press Escape
steps.expectedResult: Dropdown closes. 'Skin Care' remains as the selected value (Escape does not clear a previously confirmed selection). Focus returns to the Category dropdown.

steps.action: Repeat steps 1-5 for the 'Application Type' dropdown
steps.expectedResult: Application Type dropdown behaves identically: Escape closes without selecting, Enter confirms selection, and focus management is consistent

postconditions: Escape key consistently closes dropdowns without unintended side effects
Focus is properly managed and returns to the dropdown trigger after closing
Previously confirmed selections are not lost when Escape is pressed

accessibility.title: Touch target sizes for dropdown fields and Save button meet minimum 44x44px requirement on mobile
preconditions: User is logged in and on the cosmetic classification form page
Testing is performed on a mobile device or using browser DevTools mobile emulation (e.g., iPhone 12, Samsung Galaxy S21)
Touch interaction is the primary input method

steps.action: Open the cosmetic classification form on a mobile device or in mobile emulation mode
steps.expectedResult: The form renders in a mobile-responsive layout

steps.action: Using DevTools, inspect the 'Category' dropdown element and measure its rendered touch target size (height and width)
steps.expectedResult: The Category dropdown touch target is at least 44x44 CSS pixels (per WCAG 2.1 SC 2.5.5 Target Size)

steps.action: Inspect the 'Application Type' dropdown element and measure its touch target size
steps.expectedResult: The Application Type dropdown touch target is at least 44x44 CSS pixels

steps.action: Inspect the 'Save' button and measure its touch target size
steps.expectedResult: The Save button touch target is at least 44x44 CSS pixels

steps.action: Attempt to tap each control (Category, Application Type, Save) on the mobile device to verify they are easily activatable without accidental taps on adjacent elements
steps.expectedResult: Each control activates on the first tap without accidentally triggering adjacent controls. Sufficient spacing exists between interactive elements.

steps.action: Trigger validation errors on mobile by tapping Save with empty fields, and verify error messages are readable and tappable (if they contain links)
steps.expectedResult: Validation error messages are displayed in a readable font size and any interactive error links have touch targets of at least 44x44 CSS pixels

postconditions: All interactive elements meet minimum touch target size requirements for mobile accessibility
The form is fully operable via touch on mobile devices
Validation errors are accessible and readable on mobile screens
